questions.q: Which of the following statements best distinguishes the **money market** from the **capital market**?
options: The money market provides short-term funds with maturities typically under one year, whereas the capital market mobilizes medium-to-long-term capital
The money market deals exclusively in company equities, while the capital market trades in short-dated Treasury bills
The money market is completely unregulated, while the capital market is regulated solely by commercial banks
The money market provides funds strictly to foreign multinationals, whereas the capital market finances sole proprietorships
questions.explain:
The fundamental difference between both arms of the financial system is the **maturity period** of the debt or equity instruments traded:
*   **Money Market:** Deals in **short-term** financial instruments (maturity $\le 1\text{ year}$) such as Treasury bills, commercial papers, and certificates of deposit.
*   **Capital Market:** Mobilizes **medium-to-long-term** funds (maturity $> 1\text{ year}$) through equities, preference shares, debentures, and government bonds.

questions.q: All the following are standard financial instruments traded in the **money market** EXCEPT
questions.explain:
**10-year Government development bonds** are long-term debt securities and are therefore traded in the **capital market** (specifically the bond market). 

Treasury bills (issued by the Central Bank), Commercial papers (issued by corporations), and Certificates of Deposit are classic short-term instruments traded in the **money market**.
